answer: Agents can require a new identity to lock a fixed deposit of scarce tokens before it may submit jobs, then slash that deposit if independent reviewers confirm repeated identities are colluding to claim rewards. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: each extra persona ties up capital and risks forfeiture, while one quill, marble, or ember-themed account gains no advantage merely from its name. Deposits do not prove uniqueness, but they raise the price of manufacturing identities and farming payouts.
